title: Acme Financials - Post Pen-test Walkthrough & Patch Cadence
next_steps: Redwood to send full pen-test PDF and remediation tracker (by 2025-03-07)
Customer to provide SOC 2 Type II cert copy and scoping doc (by 2025-03-10)
Follow-up call to validate patch verification and retest plan (schedule for week of 2025-03-17)
action_items: Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Produce remediation mapping doc mapping each finding to code/component and recommended mitigation (due 2025-03-12)
Alex Kim (Redwood AE): Share SOC2/ISO evidence links and contact for KMS integration (due 2025-03-07)
Laila Ortiz (Acme Sec Eng): Provide list of internal SLAs for vulnerability remediation and the current backlog status (due 2025-03-09)
Tom Wu (Acme Platform): Confirm patch window constraints and maintenance windows for Dedicated hosts (due 2025-03-10)
topics: Audit logs and retention for compliance
summary: Post-penetration test sync between Redwood and Acme Financials. Reviewed high-level findings (one critical, three medium, several low), agreed remediation owners and timelines, discussed secure SDLC and dependency scanning gaps, clarified patch cadence constraints for the customers Dedicated nodes, and next steps to share artifacts and schedule retest. Acme emphasized need for KMS/HSM integration and stronger audit log retention for SOC2 evidence.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Jensen (CISO, Acme), Laila Ortiz (Security Eng, Acme), Tom Wu (Platform Lead, Acme)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Well do a quick roll call — Alex and Priya on the Redwood side.
[00:08] Mark (Acme): Mark here. Laila and Tom with me.
[00:12] Alex: Cool. So agenda: walk through the pen test report you shared, call out critical items, sync on patch cadence and remediation SLAs, and cover encryption/KMS questions you had. We also want to capture next steps and timing.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): Quick note, were looking at the report version v1.2 that you uploaded to the portal, right? The file named acme-pen-test-2025-v1.pdf?
[00:35] Laila (Acme): Yes, thats the one. Sent it yesterday. Some of the vuln numbers are duplicate because of different scanners so apologies for noise.
[00:44] Priya: No worries. Well try to group duplicates. To start high level, we saw one finding flagged as "critical" — unauthenticated access to the admin metrics endpoint on Dedicated hosts, correct?
[00:55] Laila: Correct. It was reproducible without auth on our test env, CVE lookalike was in the report but its an internal misconfig not an upstream CVE.
[01:05] Tom (Acme): Thats right, we had an older default config persisted on a few Dedicated hosts.
[01:10] Alex: Ok, that aligns with our notes. For that critical item, is the immediate plan to block access via network ACLs and rotate the service credentials, or do you want Redwood to push a config patch if we have access?
[01:22] Mark: We prefer to do lateral controls ourselves — network ACL first — but wed like Redwood to provide a short playbook so our ops team can implement the exact steps.
[01:30] Priya: Absolutely. We can produce a playbook with CLI snippets and a one-click runbook for Dedicated customers — will include the exact env vars, the config flags to change, and verification steps (well include a curl-based check).
[01:43] Laila: Thatd be helpful. Also we flagged some medium findings around older dependencies in the inference runtime image — e.g., libssl version mismatch and a few python package vulnerabilities.
[01:53] Priya: Right. For images, our secure SDLC includes automated dependency scanning during CI; it looks like a couple of image builds slipped through before the scanner rules were tightened.
[02:03] Tom: Can you clarify how often Redwood does base-image rebuilds and what your patch cadence is for those? Our maintenance windows are tight so we want to understand how disruptive upgrades might be.
[02:15] Priya: We do base-image rebuilds weekly for hosted clusters; for Dedicated and Private, we provide monthly patch bundles by default, and urgent security patches are done out-of-band with coordination. But we can accelerate cadence for customers with stricter SLAs — that would be part of a Dedicated contract addendum.
[02:31] Mark: Important for us: we need to guarantee remediation timelines for P1/P2 up to board level for SOC2. What are Redwoods SLAs around remediation of critical findings on Dedicated infra?
[02:42] Alex: Our standard is: when a critical is identified in our managed stack, we commit to a 72-hour mitigation window for hosted; for Dedicated, we provide a documented plan within 48 hours and coordinate a patch within the next maintenance window, unless you opt for our emergency patching add-on which can be <24 hours. Well include this in the remediation mapping.
[02:59] Laila: Please put that in writing. Well need it for our vendor risk assessment.
[03:04] Alex: Will do.
[03:08] Priya: Moving on, the report mentions weak RBAC rules and overly-broad service accounts in the monitoring namespace. Is that accurate?
[03:15] Laila: Yes, we found a service account granting cluster-admin to a metrics collector pod — it was a mistake from an older deployment template.
[03:23] Priya: Ok, thats straightforward: rotate to least-privilege role bindings and audit the namespace. We can provide an RBAC hardening guide and a simple kube-bench style checklist.
[03:33] Tom: Do you integrate with our SSO/SAML provider for user mapping? We use Okta and want to make sure role attribution is preserved in logs.
[03:41] Alex: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for accounts; role mapping is configurable and we capture identity in audit logs. We can show the exact claim names and a sample assertion.
[03:51] Mark: Audit log retention is a separate ask. For SOC2 we need 1 year of immutable logs and a tamper-evident storage option. What can Redwood provide?
[04:02] Priya: We have default 90-day retention for hosted logs in the console, but for Dedicated/Private we support configurable retention up to 3 years. For immutability, we integrate with append-only storage or can push to your SIEM. We also support KMS-wrapped signing of log batches for tamper evidence.
[04:18] Laila: So for us the ask is: provide S3-backed immutable logs with server-side encryption using our KMS keys, and a signed manifest for monthly retention snapshots. Is that possible?
[04:27] Priya: Yes, we can push logs to your S3 bucket and use your KMS key via cross-account role binding. Well outline the exact ARN perms in the integration doc.
[04:36] Mark: On KMS, were evaluating HSM-backed keys for key material. Does Redwood support AWS CloudHSM or customer-managed HSMs?
[04:44] Alex: We support customer-managed KMS keys in AWS, GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault. For CloudHSM-backed CMKs weve done integrations — its typically part of Private deployments. Well include an HSM integration reference architecture.
[04:57] Tom: Great. Back to vulnerabilities: you mentioned dependency scanning in CI. Do you block merges on critical alerts?
[05:05] Priya: Our default pipelines fail the build on high/critical CVEs for direct dependencies and open remediation tickets for transitive ones. We can provide your team the pipeline config snippets (Jenkins/GitHub Actions).
[05:16] Laila: Can we get a list of current ticketed vulnerabilities that map to the items in the pen-test report? Itll help us prioritize.
[05:24] Priya: Yes, thats part of the remediation mapping doc — well crosswalk each finding to a ticket (internal tracker ID) and include proposed mitigations and risk rating.
[05:33] Alex: Quick question from the AE side: any procurement/legal items you need to see related to incident notification and breach timelines?
[05:40] Mark: We want to confirm your notification SLA — 24 hours for confirmed breaches, 72 hours for suspected data exfil? We can feed exact wording from our vendor team.
[05:49] Alex: Redwoods standard contract includes 24-hour notification for incidents impacting confidentiality. For suspected exfil we commit to 72-hour escalation; we can align contract language.
[05:58] Mark: Ok please send that clause.
[06:02] Priya: A couple of technical clarifications from the report: the "admin metrics" issue was reproducible on port 9101 on a subset of hosts — can you confirm the host count?
[06:11] Tom: We counted 7 hosts with the legacy config out of 120 Dedicated nodes.
[06:17] Priya: Ok 7/120 is helpful. Well prioritize those for immediate ACLs and provide the verification checks.
[06:25] Laila: Theres also a medium around insecure TLS ciphers in internal service-to-service connections. We saw some servers still offering RC4 or older TLS 1.0 fallbacks in the test harness.
[06:35] Priya: We run a cipher hardening baseline during image build but older client libraries can cause fallbacks. We recommend pinning TLS policy using our runtime config and rotating the client libs; we can do a compatibility sweep with your platform team.
[06:48] Tom: That may require a canary. Our app stack is latency sensitive — upgrades need A/B canaries. How does Redwood handle canarying for runtime changes?
[06:57] Priya: We support canary routing at the model route level with traffic split, and you can pin specific hosts. Well include a canary playbook for runtime upgrade, including traffic split percentages and rollback checks.
[07:12] Mark: One procedural question: do you have a secure SDLC policy document we can reference for vendor risk? Wed like to show auditors your process for dev, code review, SCA, and pen test cadence.
[07:23] Alex: Yes we have a Secure SDLC policy and our annual pen tests plus quarterly internal scans. Well share the policy doc and a summary of past test dates.
[07:32] Laila: On the reports low findings, several were info-level items around default banners and redundant servers. Those arent a showstopper but well triage internally.
[07:41] Priya: Sounds good. For the remediation mapping, we recommend triaging criticals first, then medium, then batching low items into periodic housekeeping. Would you like Redwood to own the remediation for the components we manage?
[07:52] Mark: Wed be comfortable with Redwood remediating managed components but require approvals from our platform team prior to pushing changes into production.
[08:00] Alex: Thats standard. We will prepare change windows and require you to accept the runbook prior to execution.
[08:07] Tom: Two follow-ups: 1) will the remediation mapping include a risk-reduction estimate (percent of attack surface reduced)? 2) can we get sample test cases for the retest?
[08:18] Priya: Yes to both — well estimate risk reduction qualitatively and provide smoke test cases for each fix so you can confirm during verification.
[08:27] Laila: For retest, do you prefer we re-run the same vendor or use internal red team? We want an independent validation.
[08:33] Alex: Redwood recommends an independent retest by the vendor for continuity, but we support red-team/third-party retest as well; just coordinate timing and scope.
[08:43] Mark: Great. Can we go over the timeline and who owns what?
[08:47] Alex: Sure. Priya will produce remediation mapping and playbooks by 2025-03-12. Alex will share SOC2 evidence and the KMS/HSM integration doc by 2025-03-07. Laila will share your internal remediation SLA and backlog by 2025-03-09. Tom will confirm maintenance windows by 2025-03-10. We will schedule a follow-up week of 2025-03-17 to validate patches.
[09:10] Laila: One last question on logs: can Redwood provide hashed/signed manifests for monthly snapshots so we can prove immutability to auditors?
[09:18] Priya: Yes, we can produce a signed manifest — SHA256 plus KMS-signed envelope — and include instructions to verify signatures.
[09:26] Mark: Anything else from Redwood?
[09:29] Alex: Not from me. Well bundle the artifacts: pen-test remediation tracker, runbooks, SOC2 evidence, and the HSM integration reference. Well put links in the CRM note.
[09:41] Tom: Thanks. That should cover it.
[09:44] Mark: Thanks everyone.
[09:46] Alex: Thanks all, well follow up in writing.

Meeting end. Shared artifacts mentioned: https://redwood.example.com/artifacts/acme/pen-test-v1.2.pdf ; https://redwood.example.com/artifacts/acme/remediation-tracker.xlsx ; SOC2 link: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/soc2-type-ii.pdf

Notes on transcription: some acronyms mis-transcribed (e.g., HSM sometimes appears as "hash em"), occasional filler words removed for readability.
